content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts tend to overestimate prices in early cycles and show mean-reversion bias as prices stabilize.", "Sentiment spikes correlate with forecast overshoots, especially when bullish sentiment peaks before price reversal.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment history shows sustained positive momentum over 3–5 days.", "Model lag is evident when forecast peaks occur 2–3 days after true price peaks, indicating delayed reaction to sentiment shifts.", "Forecasts with negative sentiment at day 0 show consistent underperformance, suggesting sentiment-driven price correction.", "High forecast volatility in early cycles often precedes mean-reversion, indicating overreaction to short-term sentiment.", "Model accuracy declines when sentiment history shows mixed or declining sentiment, signaling reduced predictive power.", "Forecast bias is strongest when sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 values, indicating strong bullish momentum that is not fully reflected in model calibration."]}
